title: Scheme-theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism: affine kernels and universal property
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq Y$, the scheme-theoretic image of $h$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], with closed immersion $\iota:Z\to Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a morphism $h':X\to Z$ with $\iota\circ h'=h$, such that: (1) for every affine open $U\subseteq Y$ the ideal of $Z$ on $U$, i.e. the kernel of $\iota^\#:\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_Z(\iota^{-1}U)$, equals $\ker\big(h^\#:\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_X(h^{-1}U)\big)$; (2) for every closed immersion $i:Z'\to Y$ whose ideal is contained in that of $Z$ (on every affine open $U$, $\ker(\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_{Z'}(i^{-1}U))\subseteq\ker(\mathcal O_Y(U)\to\mathcal O_X(h^{-1}U))$) there is a unique morphism $u:X\to Z'$ with $i\circ u=h$ (uniqueness: a closed immersion is a monomorphism).
